context_requirements: Functional glycine receptor (GlyR) chloride channel expression; not established in the nine profiled lines
Neuronal or neuroendocrine lineage for canonical GlyR-mediated transcriptional effects
The annotated Drug Repurposing Hub targets for this class are muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (CHRM1-5), not glycine receptors; no evidence that these drugs act as GlyR antagonists in these lines
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Shared transcriptional signature across lines consistent with GlyR antagonism
Evidence of functional glycine receptor expression and chloride-current modulation in these lines

evidence.supports: Strychnine, a glycine receptor antagonist, blocks taurine responses in neuroendocrine cells, but the study is in flounder and does not address human cell lines or transcriptional profiling.
Kynurenic acid, a glycine receptor antagonist, improved recovery in a rat focal ischemia model; glycine receptors were upregulated in cortex, but no human cell line or landmark gene data.
Glycine prevents apoptosis of rat sinusoidal endothelial cells, but this concerns glycine as an agonist/cytoprotectant, not glycine receptor antagonism in the profiled lines.
